sentences.en: I think I was supposed to talk about my new book, which is called "Blink," and it's about snap judgments and first impressions.
sentences.zh: 我想我本该谈谈我的新书，书名叫做《倾覆》，讲的是瞬间决定和第一印象。

sentences.en: And it comes out in January, and I hope you all buy it in triplicate.
sentences.zh: 书在一月上市，我希望你们每人都买个两三本。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But I was thinking about this, and I realized that although my new book makes me happy, and I think would make my mother happy, it's not really about happiness.
sentences.zh: 不过当我想到这里时，我发现我的新书虽然使我很开心，我觉得也使我妈妈很开心，但是书本身谈的并不是快乐。

sentences.en: So I decided instead, I would talk about someone who I think has done as much to make Americans happy as perhaps anyone over the last 20 years, a man who is a great personal hero of mine:
sentences.zh: 因此我决定，我要谈一个人我认为在过去的二十年里，他为了让美国人快乐付出了比任何人都多的努力。他是我个人崇敬的一个伟大英雄。

sentences.en: someone by the name of Howard Moskowitz, who is most famous for reinventing spaghetti sauce.
sentences.zh: 他的名字是霍华德·莫斯科维茨，一个以重新发明了意粉酱而闻名的人。

sentences.en: Howard's about this high, and he's round, and he's in his 60s, and he has big huge glasses and thinning gray hair, and he has a kind of wonderful exuberance and vitality,
sentences.zh: 霍华德大概有这么高，圆圆的，他六十多岁，戴着大大的眼镜，头发稀疏灰白，不过他很有精神活力。

sentences.en: and he has a parrot, and he loves the opera, and he's a great aficionado of medieval history.
sentences.zh: 他养有一只鹦鹉，他喜欢歌剧，他还是一个中世纪历史的狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: And by profession, he's a psychophysicist.
sentences.zh: 他的职业，是精神物理学家。

sentences.en: Now, I should tell you that I have no idea what psychophysics is, although at some point in my life, I dated a girl for two years who was getting her doctorate in psychophysics.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我根本不知道精神物理学是干什么的，虽然我早年曾与一个女孩交往过两年，她当时读的就是精神物理学博士。

sentences.en: Which should tell you something about that relationship.
sentences.zh: 你也知道这段交往大概是怎么样的了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) As far as I know, psychophysics is about measuring things.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，精神物理学讲的是测量事物。霍华德很热衷于测量事物。

sentences.en: And Howard is very interested in measuring things.
sentences.zh: 他还是哈佛博士毕业的，

sentences.en: And he graduated with his doctorate from Harvard, and he set up a little consulting shop in White Plains, New York.
sentences.zh: 他在纽约州白原市设立了一个小顾问公司。他的第一个客户是… 这是很多年前的事了，在七十年代初

sentences.en: And one of his first clients was Pepsi. This is many years ago, back in the early 70s.
sentences.zh: 他最早的客户之一是百事公司。百事的人找到霍华德，说：

sentences.en: And Pepsi came to Howard and they said, "You know, there's this new thing called aspartame, and we would like to make Diet Pepsi.
sentences.zh: “你看，有一样新东西叫做阿斯巴甜，我们想要用来生产百事轻怡。

sentences.en: We'd like you to figure out how much aspartame we should put in each can of Diet Pepsi in order to have the perfect drink."
sentences.zh: 我们想要你找出在每一罐百事轻怡里放多少的阿斯巴甜，才能做出一种完美的饮料。” 对吧？

sentences.en: Now that sounds like an incredibly straightforward question to answer, and that's what Howard thought.
sentences.zh: 这个问题听上去非常地容易回答，霍华德也是这么想的。因为百事公司告诉他：

sentences.en: Because Pepsi told him, "We're working with a band between eight and 12 percent.
sentences.zh: “你看，我们测试的是从 8% 到 12% 之间的范围。

sentences.en: Anything below eight percent sweetness is not sweet enough; anything above 12 percent sweetness is too sweet.
sentences.zh: 8% 以下的甜度不够甜，12% 以上的甜度太甜了。

sentences.en: We want to know: what's the sweet spot between 8 and 12?"
sentences.zh: 我们想要知道，8% 到 12% 之间最完美的甜度是什么？”

sentences.en: Now, if I gave you this problem to do, you would all say, it's very simple.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在把这个问题交给你，你会说：这个还不简单？

sentences.en: What we do is you make up a big experimental batch of Pepsi, at every degree of sweetness -- eight percent, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, all the way up to 12 -- and we try this out with thousands of people, and we plot the results on a curve,
sentences.zh: 我们只要做出一系列不同甜度的百事，8%，8.1%，8.2,%，8.3%，一直到 12% 为止。然后我们让几千人来品尝，将结果画成一个曲线图，

sentences.en: and we take the most popular concentration, right?
sentences.zh: 最后取最多人喜欢的甜度。对吧？简单得很。

sentences.en: Really simple. Howard does the experiment, and he gets the data back, and he plots it on a curve, and all of a sudden he realizes it's not a nice bell curve.
sentences.zh: 霍华德做了这个实验，他拿到数据，然后画成一个曲线图，然后他突然发现：这并不是一个漂亮的钟形曲线。

sentences.en: In fact, the data doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些数据根本毫无逻辑。

sentences.en: It's a mess. It's all over the place. Now, most people in that business, in the world of testing food and such, are not dismayed when the data comes back a mess.
sentences.zh: 根本就是一团糟。那个行业里的大多数人，做食品测试之类的，对于一团糟的数据并不会很在意。

sentences.en: They think, "Well, you know, figuring out what people think about cola's not that easy."
sentences.zh: 他们想：你看，弄明白人们对可乐的看法不是那么简单的。

sentences.en: "You know, maybe we made an error somewhere along the way."
sentences.zh: 你看，说不定我们中途犯了一个错误。

sentences.en: "You know, let's just make an educated guess," and they simply point and they go for 10 percent, right in the middle.
sentences.zh: 我们合理猜想一下就算了，于是他们就随便地选定 10%，正正中央。

sentences.en: Howard is not so easily placated. Howard is a man of a certain degree of intellectual standards.
sentences.zh: 霍华德可不那么容易妥协。霍华德是一个有着相当程度学术标准的人。

sentences.en: And this was not good enough for him, and this question bedeviled him for years.
sentences.zh: 他对此并不满意，于是这个问题困扰了他很多年。

sentences.en: And he would think it through and say, "What was wrong?
sentences.zh: 他总会沉思良久，然后问：哪出错了呢？

sentences.en: Why could we not make sense of this experiment with Diet Pepsi?"
sentences.zh: 为什么我们弄不明白百事轻怡的这个实验呢？

sentences.en: And one day, he was sitting in a diner in White Plains, about to go trying to dream up some work for Nescafé.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他坐在白原市的一家小餐馆里，正准备要帮雀巢公司做一些工作。

sentences.en: And suddenly, like a bolt of lightning, the answer came to him.
sentences.zh: 突然间，灵光一现，他找到了答案。

sentences.en: And that is, that when they analyzed the Diet Pepsi data, they were asking the wrong question.
sentences.zh: 那就是：他们在分析百事轻怡的数据时，问的是一个错误的问题。

sentences.en: They were looking for the perfect Pepsi, and they should have been looking for the perfect Pepsis.
sentences.zh: 他们想要寻找一种最完美的百事，但他们要找的应当是多种完美的百事。相信我。

sentences.en: Trust me. This was an enormous revelation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的启示。

sentences.en: This was one of the most brilliant breakthroughs in all of food science.
sentences.zh: 这是食品科学中最了不起的突破之一。于是霍华德马上踏上了旅程，

sentences.en: Howard immediately went on the road, and he would go to conferences around the country, and he would stand up and say, "You had been looking for the perfect Pepsi.
sentences.zh: 他参加了全国各地的研讨会，站出来说：你们之前找的是一种最完美的百事。你们错了。

sentences.en: You're wrong. You should be looking for the perfect Pepsis."
sentences.zh: 你们要找的应当是多种完美的百事。”

sentences.en: And people would look at him blankly and say, "What are you talking about? Craziness."
sentences.zh: 人们面无表情地看着他，然后说：“你在胡说什么啊？神经病。”

sentences.en: And they would say, "Move! Next!" Tried to get business, nobody would hire him -- he was obsessed, though, and he talked about it and talked about it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们叫道：“让开！下一个！”他四处找生意，没有人肯雇佣他… 不过他依旧痴迷于他的想法，他不断地谈论谈论再谈论它。

sentences.en: Howard loves the Yiddish expression "To a worm in horseradish, the world is horseradish."
sentences.zh: 霍华德很喜欢一句犹太谚语：“对于一条活在辣根菜里的虫子来说，世界就是辣根菜。”

sentences.en: This was his horseradish. (Laughter) He was obsessed with it!
sentences.zh: 这就是他的辣根菜。他着迷了！

sentences.en: And finally, he had a breakthrough. Vlasic Pickles came to him, and they said, "Doctor Moskowitz, we want to make the perfect pickle."
sentences.zh: 终于，他有了一个突破。Vlasic Pickles 公司的人找到他，他们说：“莫斯科维茨先生… 莫斯科维茨博士，我们想要研制一种完美的酱菜。” 而他说：

sentences.en: And he said, "There is no perfect pickle; there are only perfect pickles."
sentences.zh: “世上没有一种最完美的酱菜，只有许多种完美的酱菜。”

sentences.en: And he came back to them and he said, "You don't just need to improve your regular; you need to create zesty."
sentences.zh: 他做完研究之后对他们说：“你们不单要改进你们的普通口味酱菜，你们还要推出柑皮口味。”

sentences.en: And that's where we got zesty pickles. Then the next person came to him: Campbell's Soup.
sentences.zh: 柑皮口味酱菜就是这么来的。下一个闻名而来的客户，是金宝汤公司。

sentences.en: And this was even more important. In fact, Campbell's Soup is where Howard made his reputation.
sentences.zh: 这一次更了不起。事实上，霍华德就是靠金宝汤而扬名的。

sentences.en: Campbell's made Prego, and Prego, in the early 80s, was struggling next to Ragù, which was the dominant spaghetti sauce of the 70s and 80s.
sentences.zh: 金宝汤生产 Prego 牌意粉酱，在八十年代初期，Prego 和 Ragu 竞争得不相上下。Ragu 牌意粉酱在七八十年代占据了市场主导地位。

sentences.en: In the industry -- I don't know whether you care about this, or how much time I have to go into this.
sentences.zh: 现在这行业里… 我不知道你是不是知道这个，或者说我要多花些时间讲详细些。

sentences.en: But it was, technically speaking -- this is an aside -- Prego is a better tomato sauce than Ragù.
sentences.zh: 不过，技术上来说，顺带一提，Prego 意粉酱比 Ragu 要好。

sentences.en: The quality of the tomato paste is much better; the spice mix is far superior; it adheres to the pasta in a much more pleasing way.
sentences.zh: 番茄酱质量更好，调味料也好多了，拌意粉吃起来更可口。事实上，

sentences.en: In fact, they would do the famous bowl test back in the 70s with Ragù and Prego.
sentences.zh: 他们在七十年代用 Ragu 和 Prego 做过著名的面盘试验。

sentences.en: You'd have a plate of spaghetti, and you would pour it on, right?
sentences.zh: 你拿一盘意粉，然后淋上意粉酱。

sentences.en: And the Ragù would all go to the bottom, and the Prego would sit on top.
sentences.zh: Ragu 会一直渗到盘底，而 Prego 会留在上面。

sentences.en: That's called "adherence." And, anyway, despite the fact that they were far superior in adherence, and the quality of their tomato paste, Prego was struggling.
sentences.zh: 这叫做“粘稠”。言归正传，尽管他们的意粉酱更粘稠，番茄酱的质量更好，Prego 却在挣扎求存。

sentences.en: So they came to Howard, and they said, fix us.
sentences.zh: 于是他们找到霍华德，说：帮我们。

sentences.en: And Howard looked at their product line, and he said, what you have is a dead tomato society.
sentences.zh: 霍华德看了他们的产品线，说：“你们这是个半死不活的番茄帝国。”

sentences.en: So he said, this is what I want to do. And he got together with the Campbell's soup kitchen, and he made 45 varieties of spaghetti sauce.
sentences.zh: 于是他说：“我打算这么干。”他和金宝汤公司一起，做出了45种不同口味的意粉酱。他用了

sentences.en: And he varied them according to every conceivable way that you can vary tomato sauce: by sweetness, by level of garlic, by tomatoey-ness, by tartness, by sourness, by visible solids -- my favorite term in the spaghetti sauce business.
sentences.zh: 一切想象得出的变量区分出这些口味。甜度，大蒜多少，辣度，酸度，番茄多少还有可见固体——番茄酱行业中我最喜欢的词汇。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Every conceivable way you can vary spaghetti sauce, he varied spaghetti sauce.
sentences.zh: 一切你想象得出的区分意粉酱的方法，他都用尽了。

sentences.en: And then he took this whole raft of 45 spaghetti sauces, and he went on the road.
sentences.zh: 然后他带上这一系列45种口味的意粉酱，踏上了旅程。

sentences.en: He went to New York, to Chicago, he went to Jacksonville, to Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 他去了纽约，他去了芝加哥，他去了杰克逊维尔，

sentences.en: And he brought in people by the truckload into big halls.
sentences.zh: 他去了洛杉矶。他将一车又一车的人带进大厅里，

sentences.en: And he sat them down for two hours, and over the course of that two hours, he gave them ten bowls.
sentences.zh: 让他们坐上两个小时，在这两个小时里，他给每人十个盘子。

sentences.en: Ten small bowls of pasta, with a different spaghetti sauce on each one.
sentences.zh: 十小盘意粉，每盘一种不同的意粉酱。

sentences.en: And after they ate each bowl, they had to rate, from 0 to 100, how good they thought the spaghetti sauce was.
sentences.zh: 他们每吃完一盘，就打分，0 到 100，评他们认为这意粉酱有多好。

sentences.en: At the end of that process, after doing it for months and months, he had a mountain of data about how the American people feel about spaghetti sauce.
sentences.zh: 最后，在经过成年累月的工作之后，他有了堆积如山的数据关于美国人对意粉酱的看法。

sentences.en: And then he analyzed the data. Did he look for the most popular variety of spaghetti sauce?
sentences.zh: 然后他分析这些数据。他找的是一种最受欢迎的意粉酱口味吗？不是！

sentences.en: No! Howard doesn't believe that there is such a thing.
sentences.zh: 霍华德不相信这东西的存在。

sentences.en: Instead, he looked at the data, and he said, let's see if we can group all these different data points into clusters.
sentences.zh: 相反，他看着这些数据，说：“看看我们能不能将这些不同的数据点归类到不同的群集里。

sentences.en: Let's see if they congregate around certain ideas.
sentences.zh: 看看这些群集能不能给我们一些启发。

sentences.en: And sure enough, if you sit down, and you analyze all this data on spaghetti sauce, you realize that all Americans fall into one of three groups.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你坐下仔细分析这些意粉酱的数据，你就会发现全美国人可分为三组。

sentences.en: There are people who like their spaghetti sauce plain; there are people who like their spaghetti sauce spicy; and there are people who like it extra chunky.
sentences.zh: 其中有喜欢一般意粉酱的人，有喜欢辣味意粉酱的人，还有喜欢带有额外颗粒的意粉酱的人。

sentences.en: And of those three facts, the third one was the most significant, because at the time, in the early 1980s, if you went to a supermarket, you would not find extra-chunky spaghetti sauce.
sentences.zh: 在这三者中，第三个发现最有价值。因为当时，在八十年代早期，如果你走进一家超市，你找不到带有额外颗粒的意粉酱。

sentences.en: And Prego turned to Howard, and they said, "You're telling me that one third of Americans crave extra-chunky spaghetti sauce and yet no one is servicing their needs?"
sentences.zh: 于是 Prego 公司问霍华德：“你是说三分之一的美国人渴望吃上带有额外颗粒的意粉酱但没有人满足他们的需要？” 他说是！

sentences.en: And he said "Yes!" (Laughter) And Prego then went back, and completely reformulated their spaghetti sauce, and came out with a line of extra chunky that immediately and completely took over the spaghetti sauce business in this country.
sentences.zh: 于是 Prego 的人回到公司，全面重新调配了他们的意粉酱，推出了一系列带有额外颗粒的意粉酱，迅速地全面占领了这个国家的意粉酱市场。

sentences.en: And over the next 10 years, they made 600 million dollars off their line of extra-chunky sauces.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的十年中，他们的额外颗粒系列意粉酱带来了六亿美元的生意。

sentences.en: Everyone else in the industry looked at what Howard had done, and they said, "Oh my god! We've been thinking all wrong!"
sentences.zh: 这行业里其他所有人看到霍华德的成就，都说：“天哪！我们一直都想错了！”

sentences.en: And that's when you started to get seven different kinds of vinegar, and 14 different kinds of mustard, and 71 different kinds of olive oil.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我们就有了7种不同的醋，14种不同的芥末酱，和71种不同的橄榄油 ─

sentences.en: And then eventually even Ragù hired Howard, and Howard did the exact same thing for Ragù that he did for Prego.
sentences.zh: 最后连 Ragu 也雇佣了霍华德，然后霍华德帮 Ragu 做了他帮 Prego 做的一样的工作。

sentences.en: And today, if you go to a really good supermarket, do you know how many Ragùs there are?
sentences.zh: 今天，如果你走进超市，一家特别好的，你会看到 Ragu 有多少种意粉酱…你知道有多少种吗？36！

sentences.en: 36! In six varieties: Cheese, Light, Robusto, Rich & Hearty, Old World Traditional -- Extra-Chunky Garden.
sentences.zh: 六大不同的风味：奶酪，轻怡，留香，浓郁，传统，额外颗粒。

sentences.en: (Laughter) That's Howard's doing. That is Howard's gift to the American people.
sentences.zh: 那就是霍华德的成就。那就是霍华德给全美国人民的礼物。

sentences.en: Now why is that important? (Laughter) It is, in fact, enormously important.
sentences.zh: 为什么说这很重要呢？这的确至关重要。我会告诉你原因。

sentences.en: I'll explain to you why. What Howard did is he fundamentally changed the way the food industry thinks about making you happy.
sentences.zh: 霍华德所做的事从根本上改变了食品行业里关于如何取悦你的思维方式

sentences.en: Assumption number one in the food industry used to be that the way to find out what people want to eat, what will make people happy, is to ask them.
sentences.zh: 食品行业曾遵循的头号信条就是：找出人们想要吃什么的方法，找出什么能取悦人们的方法，就是问他们。

sentences.en: And for years and years and years, Ragù and Prego would have focus groups, and they would sit you down, and they would say, "What do you want in a spaghetti sauce?
sentences.zh: 年复一年，年复一年地，Ragu 和 Prego 组织小组座谈会，他们邀请人们参加，然后问：“你想要什么样的意粉酱？告诉我们你想要什么样的意粉酱。”

sentences.en: Tell us what you want in a spaghetti sauce."
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你想要什么意大利面酱。”

sentences.en: And for all those years -- 20, 30 years -- through all those focus group sessions, no one ever said they wanted extra-chunky.
sentences.zh: 在那么多年里，二三十年里所有那些小组座谈会里，从来没有人说过他们想要额外颗粒的意粉酱。

sentences.en: Even though at least a third of them, deep in their hearts, actually did.
sentences.zh: 即使是他们中至少有三分之一，在他们的内心深处，确实想要额外颗粒。

sentences.en: (Laughter) People don't know what they want!
sentences.zh: 人们不知道他们想要什么！对吧？

sentences.en: As Howard loves to say, "The mind knows not what the tongue wants."
sentences.zh: 如同霍华德常说的：“脑袋不知道舌头想要的是什么。”

sentences.en: It's a mystery! (Laughter) And a critically important step in understanding our own desires and tastes is to realize that we cannot always explain what we want, deep down.
sentences.zh: 这是一个迷！而明白我们自己的欲望和品味的关键一步是明白我们并不能总说出我们心底想要的是什么。

sentences.en: If I asked all of you, for example, in this room, what you want in a coffee, you know what you'd say?
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果我问你们在场的所有人，你们想要怎样的咖啡，

sentences.en: Every one of you would say, "I want a dark, rich, hearty roast."
sentences.zh: 你知道你们会怎么回答吗？你们所有人都会说：“我想要醇厚、浓郁的黑咖啡。”

sentences.en: It's what people always say when you ask them.
sentences.zh: 当你问人们他们想要怎样的咖啡时，他们总是会这么回答。

sentences.en: "What do you like?" "Dark, rich, hearty roast!"
sentences.zh: 你喜欢什么？醇厚、浓郁的黑咖啡！

sentences.en: What percentage of you actually like a dark, rich, hearty roast?
sentences.zh: 你们中有多少人真的喜欢醇厚、浓郁的黑咖啡？

sentences.en: According to Howard, somewhere between 25 and 27 percent of you.
sentences.zh: 按照霍华德的数据，只有 25% 到 27% 的人。

sentences.en: Most of you like milky, weak coffee. (Laughter) But you will never, ever say to someone who asks you what you want that "I want a milky, weak coffee."
sentences.zh: 你们中大多数人喜欢奶味的淡咖啡。但是别人问你喜欢什么时，你绝不会承认“我想要奶味的淡咖啡。”

sentences.en: So that's number one thing that Howard did.
sentences.zh: 这就是霍华德的第一个成就。

sentences.en: Number two thing that Howard did is he made us realize -- it's another very critical point -- he made us realize the importance of what he likes to call "horizontal segmentation."
sentences.zh: 霍华德的第二个成就，就是让我们认识到，这一点也非常重要，他让我们认识到他所谓的“横向分类”的重要。

sentences.en: Why is this critical? Because this is the way the food industry thought before Howard.
sentences.zh: 这为什么重要？因为在霍华德之前，食品行业是这么想的：

sentences.en: What were they obsessed with in the early 80s?
sentences.zh: 他们在八十年代早期热衷于什么？他们热衷于芥末酱。

sentences.en: They were obsessed with mustard. In particular, they were obsessed with the story of Grey Poupon.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他们热衷于 Grey Poupon 公司的故事。对吧？

sentences.en: Used to be, there were two mustards: French's and Gulden's.
sentences.zh: 曾经，只有两种芥末酱。French's 牌和 Gulden's 牌。

sentences.en: What were they? Yellow mustard. What's in it?
sentences.zh: 它们是怎样的？黄色芥末酱。黄色芥末酱里面有什么？

sentences.en: Yellow mustard seeds, turmeric, and paprika.
sentences.zh: 黄芥末籽，姜黄，和辣椒粉。这就是芥末酱。

sentences.en: That was mustard. Grey Poupon came along, with a Dijon.
sentences.zh: Grey Poupon 来了，推出了狄戎芥末酱。对吧？

sentences.en: Right? Much more volatile brown mustard seed, some white wine, a nose hit, much more delicate aromatics.
sentences.zh: 更浓郁的褐色芥末籽，少许冲鼻的白葡萄酒更精致的香料。然后他们怎么做？

sentences.en: And what do they do? They put it in a little tiny glass jar, with a wonderful enameled label on it, made it look French, even though it's made in Oxnard, California.
sentences.zh: 他们把它用一个小玻璃罐子装起来，贴上一个精美的彩饰标签。弄得看上去很法式，尽管它是在加州的奥克斯纳德市生产的。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And instead of charging a dollar fifty for the eight-ounce bottle, the way that French's and Gulden's did, they decided to charge four dollars.
sentences.zh: 然后他们决定把八盎司装的卖到四美元一瓶，而不是像 French's 和 Gulden's 一样卖一美元五十分。

sentences.en: And they had those ads. With the guy in the Rolls Royce, eating the Grey Poupon.
sentences.zh: 他们打出广告。广告上的人坐在劳斯莱斯里，他吃着 Grey Poupon 芥末酱，另外一辆劳斯莱斯靠了上来，

sentences.en: Another pulls up, and says, "Do you have any Grey Poupon?"
sentences.zh: 车主问：“你还有 Grey Poupon 吗？”

sentences.en: And the whole thing, after they did that, Grey Poupon takes off!
sentences.zh: 他们做了这一切之后，Grey Poupon 一跃而起！

sentences.en: Takes over the mustard business! And everyone's take-home lesson from that was that the way to make people happy is to give them something that is more expensive, something to aspire to.
sentences.zh: 占领了芥末酱市场！所有人从中学到的就是：取悦人们的方法就是提供给他们更贵的，更令人向往的产品。对吧？

sentences.en: It's to make them turn their back on what they think they like now, and reach out for something higher up the mustard hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 让他们抛弃他们现在认为自己喜欢的东西，去追求更高级别的芥末酱。

sentences.en: (Laughter) A better mustard! A more expensive mustard!
sentences.zh: 更好的芥末酱！更贵的芥末酱！

sentences.en: A mustard of more sophistication and culture and meaning.
sentences.zh: 更有深度，更有文化，更有内涵的芥末酱。

sentences.en: And Howard looked to that and said, "That's wrong!"
sentences.zh: 霍华德看到这些，说：“这不对！

sentences.en: Mustard does not exist on a hierarchy. Mustard exists, just like tomato sauce, on a horizontal plane.
sentences.zh: 芥末酱没有高低之分。芥末酱，和意粉酱一样，是在同一个平面上的。

sentences.en: There is no good mustard or bad mustard.
sentences.zh: 不存在好的芥末酱，或者不好的芥末酱。

sentences.en: There is no perfect mustard or imperfect mustard.
sentences.zh: 不存在完美的芥末酱，或者不完美的芥末酱。

sentences.en: There are only different kinds of mustards that suit different kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 只有不同种类，适合不同人群口味的芥末酱。”

sentences.en: He fundamentally democratized the way we think about taste.
sentences.zh: 他从根本上将我们对品味的看法民主化了。

sentences.en: And for that, as well, we owe Howard Moskowitz a huge vote of thanks.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们该对霍华德·莫斯科维茨再一次表示深深的谢意。

sentences.en: Third thing that Howard did, and perhaps the most important, is Howard confronted the notion of the Platonic dish.
sentences.zh: 霍华德的第三个成就，也许也是最重要的一个，就是他挑战了“理想菜肴”的概念。

sentences.en: (Laughter) What do I mean by that? (Laughter) For the longest time in the food industry, there was a sense that there was one way, a perfect way, to make a dish.
sentences.zh: 此话怎讲呢？很长一段时间里，食品行业认为每一道菜肴，都有一种完美的烹饪方法。

sentences.en: You go to Chez Panisse, they give you the red-tail sashimi with roasted pumpkin seeds in a something reduction.
sentences.zh: 你去 Chez Panisse 餐馆，他们给你红尾鱼刺身配上一个有烤瓜子和其它一些什么东西的味碟。

sentences.en: They don't give you five options on the reduction.
sentences.zh: 他们不会让你从五种味碟中选一种，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't say, "Do you want the extra-chunky reduction, or ...?"
sentences.zh: 他们不会问：“您是想要有额外颗粒的味碟呢，还是想要…不会！

sentences.en: No! You just get the reduction. Why? Because the chef at Chez Panisse has a Platonic notion about red-tail sashimi.
sentences.zh: 你只能配一种味碟。为什么呢？因为 Chez Panisse 的大厨有一套做红尾鱼刺身的完美方法。

sentences.en: "This is the way it ought to be." And she serves it that way time and time again, and if you quarrel with her, she will say, "You know what? You're wrong!
sentences.zh: 这道菜就该这么做。她总是用同样的方法做这道菜。如果你和她争论，她会说：

sentences.en: This is the best way it ought to be in this restaurant."
sentences.zh: “你懂什么？你错了！我们餐馆的做法是这道菜的最好做法。”

sentences.en: Now that same idea fueled the commercial food industry as well.
sentences.zh: 同样的观念也曾影响了整个食品行业。

sentences.en: They had a Platonic notion of what tomato sauce was.
sentences.zh: 他们有一套做番茄酱的完美方法。

sentences.en: And where did that come from? It came from Italy.
sentences.zh: 从哪来的？从意大利来的。

sentences.en: Italian tomato sauce is what? It's blended; it's thin.
sentences.zh: 意大利番茄酱是怎么样的？是混合的，稀稠的。

sentences.en: The culture of tomato sauce was thin. When we talked about "authentic tomato sauce" in the 1970s, we talked about Italian tomato sauce, we talked about the earliest Ragùs, which had no visible solids, right?
sentences.zh: 番茄酱的传统是稀稠的。我们在七十年代谈到正宗的番茄酱时，我们谈的是意大利番茄酱。我们谈的是最早的 Ragu 番茄酱。没有任何可见的固体成分，对吧。

sentences.en: Which were thin, you just put a little bit and it sunk down to the bottom of the pasta.
sentences.zh: 酱是稀稠的，你只要在意粉上浇上一点它就会渗到意粉底部。

sentences.en: That's what it was. And why were we attached to that?
sentences.zh: 它曾经是这样的。那我们为什么执着于那样的番茄酱呢？

sentences.en: Because we thought that what it took to make people happy was to provide them with the most culturally authentic tomato sauce, A.
sentences.zh: 因为我们认为要让人们快乐就要给他们最正宗的番茄酱，这是其一。

sentences.en: And B, we thought that if we gave them the culturally authentic tomato sauce, then they would embrace it.
sentences.zh: 其二，我们认为只要我们给他们正宗的番茄酱，人们就会高兴地接受它。

sentences.en: And that's what would please the maximum number of people.
sentences.zh: 那就是取悦最大多数人的方法。我们那么想的原因，也就是说，

sentences.en: In other words, people in the cooking world were looking for cooking universals.
sentences.zh: 烹饪界里人们追寻的是大众口味。

sentences.en: They were looking for one way to treat all of us.
sentences.zh: 他们寻找的是一种取悦我们所有人的方法。

sentences.en: And it's good reason for them to be obsessed with the idea of universals, because all of science, through the 19th century and much of the 20th, was obsessed with universals.
sentences.zh: 他们沉迷于共性是有原因的，因为所有科学领域，在整个19世纪和20世纪的绝大部分里，都沉迷于共性。

sentences.en: Psychologists, medical scientists, economists were all interested in finding out the rules that govern the way all of us behave.
sentences.zh: 心理学家、医学家、经济学家全都热衷于寻找支配我们行为的共通法则。

sentences.en: But that changed, right? What is the great revolution in science of the last 10, 15 years?
sentences.zh: 但那已经变了，不是吗？过去 10, 15 年里科学界最大的革新是什么？

sentences.en: It is the movement from the search for universals to the understanding of variability.
sentences.zh: 是由寻找共性到了解多样性的转变。

sentences.en: Now in medical science, we don't want to know, necessarily, just how cancer works, we want to know how your cancer is different from my cancer.
sentences.zh: 现在在医学界里，我们不一定想知道癌症的原理，我们想要知道的是你们的癌症和我的癌症有何不同。

sentences.en: I guess my cancer different from your cancer.
sentences.zh: 我想是我的癌症是和你们的癌症不同。

sentences.en: Genetics has opened the door to the study of human variability.
sentences.zh: 基因学打开了研究人类多样性的大门。

sentences.en: What Howard Moskowitz was doing was saying, "This same revolution needs to happen in the world of tomato sauce."
sentences.zh: 霍华德所做的，是在呼吁番茄酱领域也需要同样的革新。

sentences.en: And for that, we owe him a great vote of thanks.
sentences.zh: 为此，我们要向他再一次表示感谢。

sentences.en: I'll give you one last illustration of variability, and that is -- oh, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我给你们最后一个多样性的例子，那就是… 哦，不好意思。

sentences.en: Howard not only believed that, but he took it a second step, which was to say that when we pursue universal principles in food, we aren't just making an error; we are actually doing ourselves a massive disservice.
sentences.zh: 霍华德并不只相信多样性，他还更进一步地指出当我们追寻食品的共通法则时，我们不光在犯一个错误，我们还是在给自己帮倒忙。

sentences.en: And the example he used was coffee. And coffee is something he did a lot of work with, with Nescafé.
sentences.zh: 他举的例子是咖啡。他曾为咖啡做了许多工作，为雀巢咖啡。

sentences.en: If I were to ask all of you to try and come up with a brand of coffee -- a type of coffee, a brew -- that made all of you happy, and then I asked you to rate that coffee, the average score in this room for coffee would be about 60 on a scale of 0 to 100.
sentences.zh: 如果我让你们试着弄出一个牌子的咖啡，一种咖啡，一种让你们所有人满意的配方，然后我让你们给那种咖啡打分，你们给的平均分，以百分制算，会在 60 分左右。

sentences.en: If, however, you allowed me to break you into coffee clusters, maybe three or four coffee clusters, and I could make coffee just for each of those individual clusters, your scores would go from 60 to 75 or 78.
sentences.zh: 不过如果，你们让我将你们分为不同的咖啡口味组，也许分成三四组，然后我就能为你们每一组做出一种咖啡，让你们的打分从 60 提高到 75 或 78。

sentences.en: The difference between coffee at 60 and coffee at 78 is a difference between coffee that makes you wince, and coffee that makes you deliriously happy.
sentences.zh: 这 60 分的咖啡和 78 分的咖啡之间的差别就是让你望而却步的咖啡和让你喜形于色的咖啡之间的差别。

sentences.en: That is the final, and I think most beautiful lesson, of Howard Moskowitz: that in embracing the diversity of human beings, we will find a surer way to true happiness.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为霍华德·莫斯科维茨给我们的最后的，也是最美的启示。那就是接受人类的多样性，我们就能找到一条确实通往真正快乐的途径。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
